claims.text: FeNiCrCoCu can be used as a thin-film protective coating on conventional metals.
Overall high-temperature wear resistance is governed by the synergistic effects of grain size, coating composition, and coating-substrate interfacial strength.
Varying coating grain size will alter the high-temperature wear resistance of FeNiCrCoCu coatings.
Varying FeNiCrCoCu coating composition will alter high-temperature wear resistance.
Modifying coating-substrate interfacial strength will alter high-temperature wear resistance.
The effects of grain size, composition, and interfacial strength can be optimized by coupling in-situ tribometry with atomistic simulations.
The combined effects of grain size, composition, and interfacial strength determine the coating's ability to withstand high-temperature wear.
The combined effects of grain size, composition, and interfacial strength influence high-temperature corrosion resistance.
An optimal combination of grain size, composition, and interfacial strength will enhance coating wear resistance.
The optimized coating will have improved high-temperature wear resistance relative to a coating with standard grain size, standard composition, and unmodified interfacial strength.
Improved wear resistance could increase coating lifespan and performance.
The hypothesis is proposed to apply from 20 to 800 degrees Celsius.
The hypothesis is proposed to apply at sliding speeds from 0.1 to 10 m/s.
The hypothesis is proposed to apply at contact pressures from 10 to 100 MPa.
The hypothesis is proposed to apply in air, vacuum, and corrosive media.
